nodes.name: Proposition 3.5
nodes.statement:
Let $\varepsilon$, $X > 0$, $Q \ge 1/2$, $N_1, N_2, Z \gg 1$, and $\Psi_1(t), \Psi_2(t)$ be smooth functions supported $t \asymp 1$, with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j Z^j$ for $j \ge 0$. Let $q \in \mathbb{Z}_+$ and $\infty_q$ be the cusp at $\infty$ of $\Gamma_0(q)$. Then using the same notation as in 3.2,
\[
    \sum_{q \sim Q} \sum_{\substack{f \\ \lambda_f < 1/4}}^{\Gamma_0(q)}
    X^{\theta_f} 
    \left\vert 
    \sum_{n_1, n_2} \Psi_1\left(\frac{n_1}{N_1}\right) \Psi_2\left(\frac{n_2}{N_2}\right) \rho_{f\infty_q}(n_1 n_2)
    \right\vert^2 
    \ll_\varepsilon 
    Q^\varepsilon Z^5
    \left(Q + N_1 N_2\right) N_1 N_2
\]
holds for any
\begin{equation} 
    X \ll \frac{Q^2}{N_1^2 N_2}.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 3.8
Proposition 3.4
nodes.statement:
Let $N \ge 1/2$, $L, H \gg 1$, $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, and $q, \ell_1, \ell_2 \in \mathbb{Z}_+$, $a \in \mathbb{Z}$ be such that $q \gg L^2$, $\ell_1, \ell_2 \asymp L$, and $(\ell_1, \ell_2) = 1$. Let $\Phi_i(t) : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{C}$ be smooth functions supported in $t \ll 1$, with $\Phi_i^{(j)} \ll_j 1$ for all $j \ge 0$, and
\[
    a_n := \sum_{\substack{h_1, h_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \\ a(h_1 \ell_1 - h_2 \ell_2) = n}} \Phi_1\left(\frac{h_1}{H}\right) \Phi_2\left(\frac{h_2}{H}\right) e(h_1 \alpha_1 + h_2 \alpha_2).
\]
Then the tuple $(q, N, H, (a_n)_{n \sim N}, A, Y)$ satisfies 3.2, where
\[
    A := \|a_n\|_2 + \sqrt{N \left(\frac{H}{L} + \frac{H^2}{L^2}\right)}, \qquad\qquad Y := \max\left(1, \frac{NH}{|a|(H+L)L\min_i T_H(\alpha_i)}\right).
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 3.7
Lemma 4.1
Lemma 6.1
Lemma 4.2
Lemma 6.2
Proposition 4.4
nodes.statement:
Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$, $A, \varepsilon > 0$, and $M, N, x, Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 \gg 1$ satisfy $MN \asymp x$ and
\begin{equation} 
\begin{aligned}
    Q_1 &\le \frac{N}{x^\varepsilon}, 
    \\
    N^2 Q_2 Q_3^2 &\le x^{1-15\varepsilon},
    \\ 
    N^2 Q_2^5 Q_3^{2} &\le 
    x^{2-40\varepsilon}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Let $(\alpha_n), (\beta_m)$ be $1$-bounded complex sequences, such that $(\alpha_n)$ is supported on $P^-(n) \ge z_0 := x^{1/(\log\log x)^3}$ and satisfies the Siegel--Walfisz condition from 4.3. Then for any $1$-bounded complex sequences $(\gamma_{q_1}), (\lambda_{q_2}), (\nu_{q_3})$ supported on $(q_i, a) = 1$, one has
\[
    \sum_{q_1 \sim Q_1} \gamma_{q_1} \sum_{q_2 \sim Q_2} \lambda_{q_2} \sum_{q_3 \sim Q_3} \nu_{q_3} \sum_{n \sim N} \alpha_n \sum_{m \sim M} \beta_m \left(\mathbbm{1}_{mn \equiv a \ (\textnormal{mod } q)} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(mn, q) = 1}}{\varphi(q)}\right)
    \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} 
    \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}.
\]

nodes.name: Proposition 6.3
nodes.statement:
For any small enough $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that the following holds. Let $M, N, L \gg 1$, $x := MNL$, $a_1, a_2 \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$ satisfy $|a_1a_2| \le x^\delta$, $(a_1, a_2) = 1$, and $(\alpha_m)_{m \sim M}, (\beta_n)_{n \sim N}, (\gamma_\ell)_{\ell\sim L}$ be $1$-bounded complex sequences. Suppose that with $\theta := 7/32$, one has
\begin{equation} 
\begin{gathered}
    x^\varepsilon \le N, \qquad 
    NL \le x^{2/3-5\varepsilon}, \qquad 
    L \le x^{-\varepsilon} M, \qquad
    M \le R \le x^{-\varepsilon} NL, \qquad 
    N^2 L^3 \le x^{1-\varepsilon} R,
    \\
    N^{7-4\theta} L^{4-\theta} \le x^{2-2\theta-\varepsilon} R^{2+\theta}.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Then one has
\[
    \sum_{\substack{r \sim R \\ (r, a_1 a_2) = 1}} 
    \left\vert \sum_{\substack{m \sim M \\ n \sim N \\ \ell \sim L}} \alpha_m  \beta_n 
    \gamma_\ell 
    \left(\mathbbm{1}_{mn\ell \equiv a_1 \overline{a_2} \ (\textnormal{mod } r)} - \frac{\mathbbm{1}_{(mn\ell, r) = 1}}{\varphi(r)} \omega_\varepsilon(mn\ell \overline{a_1} a_2; r) \right)
    \right\vert
    \ll_{\varepsilon,a_1,a_2} x^{1-\delta}.
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3
Theorem 5.4
nodes.statement:
Let $\varepsilon = 10\delta > 0$ be sufficiently small and $A > 0$. Let $(P_1, \ldots, P_r) \in \mathbf{D}^{\textnormal{well}}_r(D)$ with $1 \le D = x^{\vartheta_0}$ and $P_i = x^{t_i}$, where $t_i$ are part of the sequence $(\varepsilon^2(1+\varepsilon^9)^j)_{j \ge 1}$. Then provided that $\vartheta_0 \le \vartheta(t_1) - \varepsilon$, for any choice of the sign $\pm$, we have
\[
    \sum_{\substack{b = p_1\cdots p_r \\ D_i < p_i \le D_i^{1+\varepsilon^9}}} \sum_{\substack{d = bc \le D \\ c \mid P(p_r) \\ (d, a) = 1}}
    \widetilde\lambda^\pm(d) \left( \pi(x; d, a) - \frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(d)} \right) \ll_{a,A,\varepsilon} \frac{x}{(\log x)^A}.
\]
Moreover, if $t_1 \le \tfrac{1}{4}$ and $r \ge 3$, then the same holds provided that $\vartheta_0 \le \vartheta(t_1, t_2, t_3) - \varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.5
nodes.statement:
Let $a \in \mathbb{Z} \setminus \{0\}$ and $A, \varepsilon > 0$, $x \ge 2$. Then there exists a large enough $C = C(a, A, \varepsilon) > 0$ such that for any $y \in [(\log x)^C, x^{1/C}]$ and $Q \le x^{5/8 - \varepsilon}$, one has
\[
    \sum_{\substack{q \le Q \\ (q, a) = 1}}
    \left\vert 
    \Psi(x, y; a, q) - 
    \frac{\Psi_q(x, y)}{\varphi(q)} \right\vert 
    \ll_{\varepsilon,A,a} 
    \frac{\Psi(x, y)}{(\log x)^A}.
\]

nodes.name: Theorem 7.1
Corollary 1.4
nodes.statement:
As $x \to \infty$, one has
\[
    \#\{p \le x : p, p+2 \text{ are prime}\} \le (3.203 + o(1))\, \Pi_2(x),
\]
where $\Pi_2(x) := \tfrac{2x}{(\log x)^2} \prod_{p > 2} \tfrac{1 - 2/p}{(1 - 1/p)^2}$ is the asymptotic predicted by Hardy--Littlewood [hardy1923problems].

nodes.name: Corollary 1.6
nodes.statement:
For any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $C > 0$ such that for any $x \ge 2$ and $y \in [(\log x)^C, x^{1/C}]$, one has
    \[
        \#\{n \le x : P^+(n), P^+(n+1) \le y\} \ll_\varepsilon \varrho(u)^{1 + 5/8-\varepsilon},
    \]
    where $u := (\log x)/\log y$ and $\varrho$ denotes the Dickman function [hildebrand1986number].
